title: Zyxel
desc: Business switches, Wi-Fi, firewalls, 4G/5G and Nebula cloud

pages.t: Zyxel Networks says it has 35 years of networking expertise and serves 150 global markets. It claims about 1 million businesses use its solutions, from startups and small firms up to large businesses.

The main categories are firewalls, security routers, switches, Wi-Fi access points, 4G/5G fixed wireless, broadband access gear for operators and in-building mobile coverage. One cloud tool, Nebula, ties much of it together.
g: Access point
A device that gives Wi-Fi coverage and connects by cable to the network.
Security router
A small-office router with built-in protection against threats.

pages.t: Zyxel lists resellers, distributors, retail stores and eCommerce partners as ways to buy. A portal called Zyxel Circle handles licence and asset management for partners. For Allnet, the buyer is the reseller or integrator.

quiz.q: Which size of customer does Zyxel say its solutions cover?
o: Startups and small business up to large business
quiz.w: Zyxel lists home, startup and small business, medium business and large business.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT one of Zyxel's main business categories?
quiz.w: Zyxel's product pages list firewalls, routers, switches, Wi-Fi, fixed wireless, broadband access and in-building coverage, not door access.

quiz.q: What is Zyxel Circle?
o: A licence and asset management portal for partners
quiz.w: Zyxel describes Circle as licence and asset management for partners.

pages.t: Zyxel's switch range goes from unmanaged plug-and-play boxes, to web-managed, to smart managed (GS1900 is one series), up to Layer 3 models for aggregation and access. There are also PoE switches and PoE injectors.
g: Unmanaged switch
A switch with nothing to configure: plug in and it works.
Layer 3
A switch that can also route between networks, used in bigger setups.
PoE
Power over Ethernet: power and data over one network cable.

pages.t: Access points come in Wi-Fi 7 and Wi-Fi 6 generations, with indoor and outdoor models. Series names include NWA (Wi-Fi 7 and 6, some PRO models), WBE (Wi-Fi 7) and WAX (Wi-Fi 6), both listed as NebulaFlex Pro. Older WAC models are 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5).

A small office needing no setup usually fits an unmanaged or web-managed switch. A site wanting more control and monitoring usually needs a smart managed one. For Wi-Fi, first ask: indoor or outdoor, and how many users.

quiz.q: A tiny office wants a switch that needs no configuration. Which type fits?
quiz.w: Unmanaged switches are plug-and-play.

quiz.q: Which Zyxel access point series name belongs to the older Wi-Fi 5 generation?
quiz.w: WAC models are 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5). WBE is Wi-Fi 7 and NWA covers Wi-Fi 7 and 6.

quiz.q: A shop wants Wi-Fi for its car park too. What do you ask first?
o: Whether it has a phone system
Indoor or outdoor models, and how many users
quiz.w: Zyxel offers outdoor access points as well as indoor ones, so the placement and number of users decide the model.

src.l: Zyxel community, Elite Pack (USG LITE 60AX, SCR 50AXE)

pages.t: Zyxel's firewall (NGFW) line is pitched as protection from malware and unauthorized applications. Security routers add built-in threat protection and unified cloud management for small offices and remote deployments. Family names include USG FLEX H, USG FLEX, ATP, USG LITE and SCR; check which are current.
g: NGFW
Next-generation firewall: filters traffic by application and threat, not just ports.
Edge
The point where the customer's network meets the internet.

pages.t: Security features such as protection services need licences. Zyxel groups them into security, management and reporting, and connectivity categories. A License Finder tool is linked from the Service and License menu on zyxel.com.
g: Licence
A paid right to use a feature, usually for a set period and renewed.

pages.t: The security router page filters models by number of users (from 5 up to 800) and by internet bandwidth. Ask the customer how many people and how fast a line they have, then match the model.

quiz.q: Which Zyxel product type suits a small branch needing built-in threat protection?
quiz.w: Security routers are described as built-in protection for small offices and remote sites.

quiz.q: Why does a firewall quote often include licences?
quiz.w: Zyxel offers security, management and connectivity licences for its security devices.

quiz.q: Which two facts help size a Zyxel security router?
o: Number of users and internet bandwidth
quiz.w: The product filters list users (5 to 800) and internet bandwidth.

pages.t: Fixed wireless access (FWA) gives broadband over mobile networks where cables are limited. Zyxel offers 4G LTE and 5G routers, both indoor and outdoor, aimed at SMBs, home offices and tech-savvy users.
g: FWA
Fixed wireless access: broadband delivered by radio instead of a cable.
LTE
The technical name for 4G mobile data.

pages.t: Several FWA models carry the Nebula name, such as Nebula FWA710 (outdoor 5G) and Nebula FWA510 (indoor 5G). Nebula describes its 4G/5G routers as cloud-managed, in the same tool as access points and switches.

Zyxel also lists fixed broadband access gear for WISPs, MSPs and regional operators, and in-building coverage for indoor cellular signal in small and mid-sized venues. These are niche: check the customer is an operator first.
g: WISP
Wireless Internet Service Provider: sells internet over radio links.
MSP
Managed service provider: a firm that runs IT for customers.

quiz.q: A pop-up store has no cable internet. What type of Zyxel product is the starting point?
quiz.w: FWA devices bring broadband over mobile networks where wired links are limited.

quiz.q: Which Zyxel line is aimed at WISPs and regional operators?
quiz.w: Zyxel lists fixed broadband access for WISPs, MSPs and regional operators.

quiz.q: What does the 'Nebula' in a model name like Nebula FWA510 tell you?
o: It can be managed in Zyxel's Nebula cloud
quiz.w: Nebula-named models are meant to be managed through the Nebula cloud platform.

src.l: Zyxel community, Elite Pack and Nebula Pro grace period

pages.t: Nebula manages access points, switches, firewalls and 4G/5G routers from one cloud screen, with a mobile app and Zero Touch Provisioning. Multi-site and multi-customer views make it handy for MSPs.
g: Zero Touch Provisioning
A new device finds the cloud and configures itself, so no one needs to set it up on site.

pages.t: Nebula has a free tier (called Base in Zyxel's 2021 licence notice) plus paid packs, such as Pro, with more control and visibility. Licences are per device, and an organisation only runs a pack level if all its devices have it. A separate MSP Pack is counted per user account.
g: Organisation
One customer's network inside Nebula, with its own devices and admins.

pages.t: Most devices work either cloud-managed or standalone. If licences lapse or a device is added without one, Nebula gives a 15-day grace period, then usually falls back to Base. Zyxel also offers pay as you go through Circle. Packs change over time: check current terms and prices with Allnet.
g: Standalone
The device is managed locally, without the cloud.

quiz.q: A reseller asks if Nebula costs anything to start. What is a correct answer?
o: Nebula has a free tier and paid packs with more features
Everything in Nebula is paid from day one
quiz.w: Zyxel describes a complimentary plan (called Base in its licence notice) and paid plans for more control.

quiz.q: How are paid Nebula licences counted?
o: One licence for any number of customers
Per device, and the whole organisation needs the same pack
quiz.w: Licensing is per device, and an organisation only runs a pack level when every device has a licence for it.

quiz.q: A customer's Pro licences expire. What happens first?
o: A 15-day grace period, then usually a drop to Base
quiz.w: Zyxel describes a 15-day grace period before the organisation falls back to the least compatible pack, typically Base.

quiz.q: An MSP wants to look after many customers. Which part is relevant?
o: Multi-customer MSP tools and the MSP Pack
quiz.w: Nebula has built-in multi-tenant tools for MSPs, plus a separate MSP Pack licence counted per user account.

pages.t: Zyxel's pitch is one vendor for the whole SMB network: firewall, switches, Wi-Fi and 4G/5G, managed from Nebula. It often suits customers with several sites, little on-site IT, or an MSP running things for them.

A single-category vendor, say Wi-Fi only, leaves the customer mixing tools. A full enterprise platform may bring more depth and cost. Zyxel often sits in between: broad range, a free cloud tier, and security from the same vendor.

How many sites and users? Is there a cable line or mobile only? Indoors or outdoors? Does an MSP manage it? Is a firewall needed? Answers pick the products. For very large or regulated projects, involve a colleague.

quiz.q: A retailer has 12 small shops, no IT staff and wants one remote view. Best Zyxel angle?
o: Firewall, switch and Wi-Fi managed together in Nebula
Only a desktop unmanaged switch per shop
quiz.w: Multi-site, one cloud view and one vendor is Zyxel's main pitch.

quiz.q: A farm shed has no cable internet and needs a connection. Which area?
quiz.w: Outdoor FWA routers bring broadband where wired links are limited.

quiz.q: What is a sensible reply to 'is Zyxel enough for a huge regulated bank?'
o: Collect requirements and involve a colleague
quiz.w: Large regulated projects need verified answers, so escalate.

quiz.q: Which statement about Zyxel versus a Wi-Fi-only vendor is fair?
o: Zyxel covers many categories under one cloud tool
quiz.w: Zyxel spans firewalls, switches, Wi-Fi and 4G/5G with Nebula.

about: Broad business networking vendor that says it has 35 years of experience and serves 150 markets. Sells firewalls, switches, Wi-Fi, 4G/5G and operator access gear.
Sold through resellers and distributors, often to customers with several sites, little on-site IT, or an MSP running the network.
Zyxel pitches one vendor for the whole small business network, managed from the Nebula cloud tool, which has a free tier.
